quote: Code smells.
author: Martin Fowler

quote: Don't live with broken windows.
author: Andy Hunt
Dave Thomas

quote: Functions should do one thing. They should do it well. They should do it only.
author: Robert C. Martin

quote: The first rule of functions is that they should be small. The second rule of functions is that they should be smaller than that.
author: Robert C. Martin

quote: The ideal numbers of arguments for a function is zero (niladic). Next comes one (monadic), followed closely by two (dyadic). Three arguments (triadic) should be avoided where possible. More than three (polyadic) requires very special justification ‐ and then shouldn't be used anyway.
author: Robert C. Martin

quote: DRY ‐ Don't Repeat Yourself ‐ Every piece of knowledge must have a single, unambiguous, authoritative representation within a system.
author: Dave Thomas
Andy Hunt

quote: Be careful to preserve the orthogonality of your system as you introduce third-party toolkits and libraries. Choose your technologies wisely.
author: Dave Thomas
Andy Hunt

quote: Don't comment bad code ‐ rewrite it.
author: P. J. Plaugher
Brian W. Kernighan

quote: Complexity kills. It sucks the life out of developers, it makes products difficult to plan, build, and test.
author: Ray Ozzie

quote:
The Three Laws of TDD:

  1) You may not write production code until you have written a failing unit test.
  2) You may not write more of a unit test than is sufficient to fail, and not compiling is failing.
  3) You may not write more production code than is sufficient to pass the currently failing test.
author: Robert C. Martin

quote: Objects are abstractions of processing. Threads are abstractions of schedule.
author: James O. Coplien

quote: Controlling complexity is the essence of computer programming.
author: Brian W. Kernighan

quote: There are two ways of constructing a software design. One way is to make it so simple that there are obviously no deficiencies. And the other way is to make it so complicated that there are no obvious deficiencies.

quote: There's an old story about the person who wished his computer were as easy to use as his telephone.  That wish has come true, since I no longer know how to use my telephone.

quote: Most of you are familiar with the virtues of a programmer. There are three, of course: laziness, impatience, and hubris.
author: Larry Wall

quote: That's the thing about people who think they hate computers.  What they really hate is lousy programmers.

quote: To iterate is human, to recurse divine.
author: L. Peter Deutsch

quote: Walking on water and developing software from a specification are easy if both are frozen.
author: Edward V. Berard

quote: The first 90% of the code accounts for the first 90% of the development time. The remaining 10% of the code accounts for the other 90% of the development time.
author: Tom Cargill

quote: If you want to set off and go develop some grand new thing, you don't need millions of dollars of capitalization. You need enough pizza and Diet Coke to stick in your refrigerator, a cheap PC to work on and the dedication to go through with it.
author: John Carmack

quote: Some people, when confronted with a problem, think “I know, I’ll use regular expressions.” Now they have two problems.

quote: There are only two kinds of languages: the ones people complain about and the ones noquote uses.
author: Bjarne Stroustrup

quote: It works on my machine.
author: anonymous

quote: If debugging is the process of removing software bugs, then programming must be the process of putting them in.

quote: Refuctoring — the process of taking a well-designed piece of code and, through a series of small, reversible changes, making it completely unmaintainable by anyone except yourself.

quote: Computer Science is no more about computers than astronomy is about telescopes.

quote: Perfection is achieved, not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away.
author: Antoine de Saint Exupéry

quote: The most exciting phrase to hear in science, the one that heralds new discoveries, is not 'Eureka!' but 'That's funny...'
author: Isaac Asimov

quote: The difference between theory and practice is smaller in theory than in practice.
author: anonymous

quote: Never trust a programmer in a suit.
author: anonymous

quote: The trouble with programmers is that you can never tell what a programmer is doing until it's too late.

quote: Rules of Optimization: Rule 1: Don't do it. Rule 2 (for experts only): Don't do it yet.
author: Michael A. Jackson

quote: It's not at all important to get it right the first time. It's vitally important to get it right the last time.

Andy Hunt

quote: You don't have a scaling problem yet.
author: 37Signals

quote: True innovation often comes from the small startup who is lean enough to launch a market but lacks the heft to own it.
author: Timm Martin

quote: Deleted code is debugged code.
author: Jeff Sickel

quote: If you're willing to restrict the flexibility of your approach, you can almost always do something better.
author: John Carmack

quote: The central enemy of reliability is complexity.
author: Daniel Geer

quote: Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability.

quote: A program is portable to the extent that it can be easily moved to a new computing environment with much less effort than would be required to write it afresh.
author: W. Stan Brown

quote: Just because the standard provides a cliff in front of you, you are not necessarily required to jump off it.
author: Norman Diamond

quote: Correctness is clearly the prime quality. If a system does not do what it is supposed to do, then everything else about it matters little.
author: Bertrand Meyer

quote: Compatibility means deliberately repeating other people's mistakes.
author: David Wheeler

quote: Premature optimization is the root of all evil in programming.
author: anonymous

quote: Testing can show the presence of errors, but not their absence.
author: E. W. Dijkstra

quote: A computer is a stupid machine with the ability to do incredibly smart things, while computer programmers are smart people with the ability to do incredibly stupid things. They are, in short, a perfect match.

quote: Profanity is the one language all programmers know best.
author: anonymous

quote: I don't care if it works on your machine! We are not shipping your machine!

quote: Each new user of a new system uncovers a new class of bugs.

quote: Encoded names are seldom pronounceable and are easy to miss-type.

quote: When you come across a stumbling block because the code doesn't quite fit anymore, or you notice two things that should really be merged, or anything else at all strikes you as being “wrong”, don't hesitate to change it. There's no time like the present.

quote: Don't waste your time typing up that long visionary tome; no one's going to read it. Take consolation in the fact that if you give your product enough room to grow itself, in the end it won't resemble anything you wrote about anyway.

quote: Always code as if the guy who ends up maintaining your code will be a violent psychopath who knows where you live.

quote: Programming is like sex: one mistake and you're providing support for a lifetime.

quote: A sentence should be enough to get the idea across.

quote: Programmer — an organism that turns coffee into software.

quote: A good programmer is someone who always looks both ways before crossing a one-way street.

quote: Managing senior programmers is like herding cats.

quote: It's better to wait for a productive programmer to become available than it is to wait for the first available programmer to become productive.

quote: Playfully doing something difficult, whether useful or not, that is hacking.

quote: It's not a bug — it's an undocumented feature.

quote: Programs must be written for people to read, and only incidentally for machines to execute.

quote: You broke the build!

author: Martin Fowler

author: Eric Raymond

quote: Every program has two purposes: The one for which it was written and another for which it wasn't.

quote: Fools ignore complexity. Pragmatists suffer it. Some can avoid it. Geniuses remove it.

author: anonymous

quote: Why do we never have time to do it right, but always have time to do it over?

quote: Don't have good ideas if you aren't willing to be responsible for them.

author: anonymous

author: Eric Raymond

quote: XML documents are much like humans — they are cute and fun to deal with when they’re small but can get really annoying as they grow bigger.

quote: I love deadlines. I like the whooshing sound they make as they fly by.

quote: Features, quality, time: pick two.

quote: JavaScript is the only language that I’m aware of that people feel they don’t need to learn before they start using it.

quote: You won't get anything done by planning.

quote: All programming languages are shit. But the good ones fertilize your mind.

quote: At some point software design becomes less about what and more about when.

quote: Programming uses head and gut.

quote: Linux is only free if your time has no value.

quote: If we have data, let’s look at data. If all we have are opinions, let’s go with mine.

quote: Write code every day.
author: John Resig

quote: Sure I could program in PHP, but I could also use a sundial to tell time.

quote: Node.js is a tumor on the programming community, in that not only is it completely braindead, but the people who use it go on to infect other people who can't think for themselves.

quote: The problem with object-oriented languages is they’ve got all this implicit environment that they carry around with them. You wanted a banana but what you got was a gorilla holding the banana and the entire jungle.

quote: Object-oriented design is the roman numerals of computing.
author: Rob Pike

quote: The most important property of a program is whether it accomplishes the intention of its user.

quote: You cannot manage that which you cannot measure.

quote: Nine people can’t make a baby in a month.
author: Frederick P. Brooks

quote: You do not really understand something unless you can explain it to your grandmother.

quote: Simple doesn't mean stupid. Thinking that it does, does.

author: Eric Ries

quote: If McDonald's were run like a software company, one out of every hundred Big Macs would give you food poisoning, and the response would be, “We're sorry, here is a coupon for two more”.

author: Ken Thompson

quote: The best way to prepare [to be a programmer] is to write programs, and to study great programs that other people have written. In my case, I went to the garbage cans at the Computer Science Center and fished out listings of their operating system.
author: Bill Gates

quote: Users who want critical bug fixes and new features without actually upgrading their software also want magic flying candy-dropping ponies.
author: chromatic

quote: Feature-based releases expand to fill all available time until someone feels guilty for not finishing the feature on a magical, wish-fulfillment schedule, and hey, has it been a couple of years already?
author: chromatic

quote: Do not use humans for jobs computers can do better — this is a waste of human energy and creativity, the only real resource on this planet, and demeans the human spirit.
author: J. Paul Morrison

quote: A generalist is a jack-of-all-trades but a master of none, whereas a generalizing specialist is a jack-of-all-trades and master of a few. Big difference.
author: Scott Ambler

quote: A human being should be able to change a diaper, plan an invasion, butcher a hog, conn a ship, design a building, write a sonnet, balance accounts, build a wall, set a bone, comfort the dying, take orders, give orders, cooperate, act alone, solve equations, analyze a new problem, pitch manure, program a computer, cook a tasty meal, fight efficiently, die gallantly. Specialization is for insects.
author: Robert A. Heinlein

quote: The amount of energy necessary to refute bullshit is an order of magnitude bigger than to produce it.
author: Alberto Brandolini

quote: Not all eyes that notice bugs in Open Source code belong to saints who will report or repair them in the interest of the public good.
author: Martin Fowler

quote: It's a lot easier to talk about code than it is to write code.
author: John O'Nolan

quote: If you are choosing a JavaScript library purely based on popularity, I think you deserve what you get.
author: Tom Dale

quote: What exactly makes a great platform? It’s about what your business puts into its platform and what your consumers and/or business partners get out of it. And that’s the point. A platform either fits into an overall corporate strategy or it doesn’t.
author: Phil Simon

quote: Easy is not to be underestimated. Easy taps the pool of talent and ideas out there that were turned off by hard.
author: Chris Anderson

quote: Most of the biggest problems in software are problems of misconception.
author: Rich Hickey

quote: As a Lead JavaScript Engineer, I try to get my team to write as little JavaScript as possible.
author: anonymous

quote: Get out of the way of your developers or lose them to someone who will.
author: Adrian Cockcroft

quote: A person without data is just another person with an opinion.
author: anonymous

quote: Programs, like people, get old. We can’t prevent ageing, but we can understand its causes, limit its effects and reverse some of the damage.
author: Mario Fusco

quote: If you're actually doing TDD, you're throwing away tests all the time, as your understanding of what the code is changes.
author: Kerri Miller

quote: Simplicity is about subtracting the obvious and adding the meaningful.
author: John Maeda

quote: Programmers are as emotional and irrational as normal people.
author: Douglas Crockford

quote: Blame the implementation, not the technique.
author: Tim Kadlec

quote: What matters for simplicity is that there's not interleaving.
author: Rich Hickey

quote: The art of programming is the art of organizing complexity, of mastering multitude and avoiding its bastard chaos as effectively as possible.
author: E. W. Dijkstra

quote: Scrum is like the rules of soccer. Following them does not make you a good player.
author: Jeff Sutherland

quote: Writing software as if we are the only person that ever has to comprehend it is one of the biggest mistakes and false assumptions that can be made.
author: Karolina Szczur

quote: The craft of programming begins with empathy, not formatting or languages or tools or algorithms or data structures.
author: Kent Beck

quote: I hate code, and I want as little of it as possible in our product.
author: Jack Diederich

quote: It's important to remember that when you start from scratch there is absolutely no reason to believe that you are going to do a better job than you did the first time. First of all, you probably don't even have the same programming team that worked on version one, so you don't actually have “more experience”. You're just going to make most of the old mistakes again, and introduce some new problems that weren't in the original version.
author: Joel Spolsky

quote: The key is to acknowledge from the start that you have no idea how this will grow. When you accept that you don't know everything, you begin to design the system defensively... You should spend most of your time thinking about interfaces rather than implementations.
author: Nicholas Zakas

quote: A program is like a poem: you cannot write a poem without writing it.
author: E. W. Dijkstra

quote: Security is a state of mind.
author: NSA Security Manual

quote: Languages that try to disallow idiocy become themselves idiotic.
author: Rob Pike

quote: When in doubt, leave it out.
author: Joshua Bloch

quote: No code is faster than no code.
author: merb motto

quote: Data dominates. If you’ve chosen the right data structures and organized things well, the algorithms will almost always be self-evident. Data structures, not algorithms, are central to programming.
author: Rob Pike

quote: The best reaction to “this is confusing, where are the docs” is to rewrite the feature to make it less confusing, not write more docs.
author: Jeff Atwood

quote: Treat your code like poetry and take it to the edge of the bare minimum.
author: Ilyo

quote:
There is no single development, in either technology or management
technique, which by itself promises even one order-of-magnitude
improvement within a decade in productivity, in reliability, in simplicity.
author: Frederick P. Brooks

quote: And the reason these things take a generation is because ultimately we do not change people's minds. We have to wait for the previous generation to retire or die before we can get critical mass on the next idea. So it's like we look around: “Are they gone?”
author: Douglas Crockford

quote: Big data is like teenage sex: everyone talks about it, noquote really knows how to do it, everyone thinks everyone else is doing it, so everyone claims they are doing it...
author: Dan Ariely

quote: Good engineers make solutions obsolete. Great engineers make themselves obsolete.
author: Jordan W

quote: Organizations which design systems are constrained to produce designs which are copies of the communication structures of these organizations.
author: Conway's law

quote: Always bet on JavaScript.
author: Brendan Eich

quote: Things that are impossible just take longer.
author: Ian Hickson

quote: Well-designed components are easy to replace. Eventually, they will be replaced by ones that are not so easy to replace.
author: Sustrik's Law

quote: Programmers are often angry because they’re often scared.
author: Paul Ford

quote: (...) Thinking this way will teach you two things about computers: One, there’s no magic, no matter how much it looks like there is. There’s just work to make things look like magic. And two, it’s crazy in there.
author: Paul Ford

quote: A Fallacy of Software: If it works, and we don't change anything, it will keep working.
author: Jessica Kerr

quote: Almost without exception, the best products are developed by teams with desire to solve a problem; not a company's need to fulfil a strategy.
author: Jeff Weiner

quote: The best error message is the one that never shows up.
author: Thomas Fuchs

quote: Telling a programmer there's already a library to do X is like telling a songwriter there's already a song about love.
author: Pete Cordell

quote: A programmer does not primarily write code; rather, he primarily writes to another programmer about his problem solution. The understanding of this fact is the final step in his maturation as technician.
author: anonymous

quote: It can be better to copy a little code than to pull in a big library for one function.  Dependency hygiene trumps code reuse.
author: Rob Pike

quote: There's nothing more permanent than a temporary hack.
author: Kyle Simpson

quote: Like designers, if you give a programmer a problem with parameters, they’ll apply every bit of genius they have to solve it in the best possible way. If you tell them how to do it, you’ll suffer the wrath of an angry God.
author: Derek Powazek

quote: Start out with finding the right problem to solve. This is a combination of “what customers are asking for”, “what customers don’t even know they want yet” and “what can be solved with something simple to understand and manage”
author: Radia Perlman

quote: Teams are immutable. Every time someone leaves, or joins, you have a new team, not a changed team.
author: Richard Dalton

quote: Every great developer you know got there by solving problems they were unqualified to solve until they actually did it.
author: Patrick McKenzie

quote: That which optimizes one part of the system necessarily undermines the system as a whole.
author: Eric Ries

quote: Hardware eventually fails. Software eventually works.
author: Michael Hartung

quote: We crave for new sensations but soon become indifferent to them. Wonders of yesterday are today common occurrences.
author: Nikola Tesla

quote: I know testers who make good devs. I know devs who make good testers. I know Scrum Masters who make good coffee.
author: David Evans

quote: Go is the language JavaScript programmers retire to when they get old. Like the Florida of programming languages.
author: Jed Schmidt

quote: UNIX is simple. It just takes a genius to understand its simplicity.
author: Dennis M. Ritchie

quote: An evolving system increases its complexity unless work is done to reduce it.
author: Meir Lehman

quote: Almost every attempt at making something better will be regarded by someone else as a personal attack.
author: Chris Sacca

quote: The competent programmer is fully aware of the strictly limited size of his own skull; therefore he approaches the programming task in full humility, and among other things he avoids clever tricks like the plague.
author: E. W. Dijkstra

quote: Bad programmers worry about the code. Good programmers worry about data structures and their relationships.
author: Linus Torvalds

quote: 90% of the functionality delivered now is better than 100% delivered never.
author: Brian W. Kernighan
P. J. Plaugher

quote: Software being “Done” is like lawn being “Mowed”.
author: Jim Benson

quote: Promoting a good developer to management is often a twofold bad move: you'll lose a good developer and get a poor manager.
author: Mario Fusco

quote: Programmers have to fight against the two most destructive forces in the universe: entropy and stupidity.
author: Damian Conway

quote: What one programmer can do in one month, two programmers can do in two months.
author: Frederick P. Brooks

quote: If you say “I told you so”, you are the one who has failed. Because you knew, but did not manage to stop the train wreck.
author: Robert C. Martin

quote: These days, the problem isn't how to innovate; it's how to get society to adopt the good ideas that already exist.
author: Douglas Engelbart

quote: In carpentry you measure twice and cut once. In software development you never measure and make cuts until you run out of time.
author: Adam Morse

quote: A good API is not just easy to use but also hard to misuse.
author: JBD

quote: The best way to get the right answer on the internet is not to ask a question; it's to post the wrong answer.
author: Cunningham's Law

quote: Programming is not easy like Sunday morning, it is silent poetry.
author: Waseem Latif

quote: Formal education will make you a living. Self-education will make you a fortune.
author: Jim Rohn

quote: Code is like humor. When you have to explain it, it’s bad.
author: Cory House

quote: Terrible code is not a good excuse to be mean, because terrible code is not well-correlated with having been written by terrible people.
author: GeePaw Hill

quote: A computer is like a mischievous genie. It will give you exactly what you ask for, but not always what you want.
author: Joe Sondow

quote: Programming is just saying “I have a meeting in an hour so better not start on this yet” to yourself until you die.
author: Alex Engelberg

quote: Once a new technology rolls over you, if you're not part of the steamroller you're part of the road.
author: Stewart Brand

quote: The amateur software engineer is always in search of magic.
author: Grady Booch

quote: Programming languages, like pizza, come in only two sizes: too big and too small.
author: Richard Pattis

quote: The only way to learn a new programming language is by writing programs in it.
author: Dennis M. Ritchie

quote: If it doesn’t work, it doesn’t matter how fast it doesn’t work.
author: Mich Ravera

quote: Rarely is anyone thanked for the work they did to prevent the disaster that didn't happen.
author: Mikko Hypponen

quote: Java is to JavaScript as ham is to hamster.
author: Jeremy Keith

quote: I think it's very important to get more women into computing. My slogan is: Computing is too important to be left to men.
author: Karen Spärck Jones

quote: A primary cause of complexity is that software vendors uncritically adopt almost any feature that users want.
author: Niklaus Wirth

quote: No one in the brief history of computing has ever written a piece of perfect software. It's unlikely that you'll be the first.
author: Andy Hunt

quote: When you don't create things, you become defined by your tastes rather than ability. Your tastes only narrow & exclude people. So create.
author: Why The Lucky Stiff

quote: The most disastrous thing that you can ever learn is your first programming language.
author: Alan Kay

quote: The best programs are the ones written when the programmer is supposed to be working on something else.
author: Melinda Varian

quote: There are only two hard things in Computer Science: cache invalidation and naming things
author: Phil Karlton

quote: Everything in software architecture is a trade-off.
author: First Law of Software Architecture

quote: Part of the inhumanity of the computer is that, once it is competently programmed and working smoothly, it is completely honest.
author: Isaac Asimov

quote: The number one skill required for learning any complex system is patience.
author: Kelsey Hightower

quote: If you can get today’s work done today, but you do it in such a way that you can’t possibly get tomorrow’s work done tomorrow, then you lose.
author: Martin Fowler

quote: People have an enormous tendency to resist change. They love to say, 'We've always done it this way.' I try to fight that.
author: Grace Hopper
